title: Ephemeral shadow lanes with traffic-fraction decay for safer A/B and canary experiments
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: Long-lived shadow traffic is useful for fidelity checks but increases cost and surface area for unnoticed drift. This PR introduces an ephemeral shadow lane primitive with time- and signal-driven traffic-fraction decay to make shadowing suitable for routine canary/A-B validation without requiring manual cleanup. The feature is intended to: 1) preserve signal fidelity for short windows (fast smoke + fidelity checks), 2) automatically reduce shadow weight to zero if no active observation is required, and 3) integrate with existing rollout controller safety gates for automatic rollback triggers. High-level design: ephemeral shadow lanes are declared alongside canary or A/B routes in the ServeGraph. Each ephemeral shadow has a TTL and a decay profile (linear, exponential, step). The rollout controller spins up a transient shadow replica group, applies initial shadow_weight, and emits metrics against the shadow bucket. If specified safety gates (latency, error-rate, quality delta against eval set) are satisfied the controller can schedule a follow-up promotion; otherwise the decay scheduler reduces shadow_weight over the TTL until eviction. An important behavior: if a shadow's observed metric divergence exceeds thresholds, the controller immediately clamps weight to zero and records a snapshot for replay. This PR focuses on the runtime integration, decay scheduler, telemetry, and the operator API surface for declaring ephemeral shadows. It does not include a UI surface (Console work will follow). Checklist: - [x] Decay scheduler and TTL semantics implemented - [x] Integration with rollout controller and canary atoms - [x] Metrics/tracing hooks for shadow buckets (tokenized traces + summary histograms) - [x] Safety clamp on divergence with snapshot capture - [x] Unit and integration tests for scheduler edge cases - [x] Documentation of API surface and examples Implementation notes: - New runtime component: shadow-decay-scheduler (goroutine-based, backoff-aware) - Rollout controller changes: ephemeralShadow struct + reconciliation path, immediate-clamp path on threshold breach - Telemetry: added shadow_bucket.{requests,errors,latency_p95,quality_delta} and a short-lived tag ephemeral=true - Storage: lightweight snapshot persisted to objectstore for replay; snapshots are time-limited retention by default - Compatibility: when ephemeral=false the behavior is unchanged; ephemeral is opt-in via route annotations Risk & mitigation: - Race between scheduler and controller reconciliation fixed by leader-lease + compare-and-swap on shadow metadata; tests added - Increased cost during initial warmup mitigated by default small initial shadow_weight (0.05) and fast decay profiles - Potential for missed signal if TTL too short: recommended defaults: TTL=30m for smoke, 4h for extended validation Testing: See commits for unit+integration tests. Local canary harness used to simulate partial failures, injected latency, and ground-truth eval comparisons. Rollout examples included for canary and A/B scenarios. Migration plan: - Gradual rollout under feature flag rollout.ephemeral_shadow=true - Default behavior off - Announce to users with migration notes and examples in docs/rollouts/ephemeral-shadows.md Related work: ties into ENG-2110 (automated-rollout-playbooks) and ENG-2398 (shadow-promote-oracle).

review_comments: Priya Shah: Nice shape. A few concerns: how do we ensure eviction doesn't drop useful replay state? Please add retention tuning and a small integration test for snapshot replay.
Samir Patel (author): Added retention tunables with defaults and an integration test; see e6b2c4 commit. Snapshots are now GC'd after 72h by default but configurable via controller config.
Michael Torres: Can we avoid an extra RW lock by leveraging the existing deployment lease? The compare-and-swap path looks fine but prefer reusing lease semantics where possible.
Samir Patel: Reused deployment lease for leader election; left CAS for shadow metadata to prevent stale reconcilers from overriding TTL. See f2a9d8.
Hannah Li: CI failure on lint in first run, tests flaked on p95 latency assertion in the harness — was that addressed?
Samir Patel: Fixed harness timing by introducing jitter-tolerant assertion and extended p95 window for synthetic load. CI passed on rerun.
merge_summary: Merged via squash. Final commit message consolidates design notes and usage example. Post-merge tasks: Console work (UI) and opt-in feature flag rollout. Doc link added to the release notes.
release_notes: Feature: Ephemeral shadow lanes (opt-in) — allows short-lived shadow traffic with automatic decay and safety clamps for canary and A/B experiments. Controlled by rollout.ephemeral_shadow feature flag. See docs/rollouts/ephemeral-shadows.md for usage and migration guidance.
playback_instructions: To reproduce locally: 1) apply examples/canary/ephemeral-shadow.yaml, 2) enable rollout.ephemeral_shadow=true in controller config, 3) run tests/integration/ephemeral_shadow_test.go with --harness-local. Use telemetry tags ephemeral=true to filter shadow traffic metrics.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps Console surface for a follow-up to reduce scope. Operators should watch shadow_bucket.quality_delta and shadow_bucket.errors for early clamp triggers.
ci_flakiness_notes: Initial CI run failed due to timing assumptions in synthetic harness; addressed with jitter-tolerant assertions and clearer harness time scaling in integration config.
